newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight orders fly, Cuba shipments underway.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight orders fly, Cuba shipments underway.

text.p: The sugar freight market was awash with a spate of fresh inquiry on Monday as Cuba's 1996/97 sugar shipment cycle got properly underway boosted by cargoes from the latter end of the north Brazilian crop, shipbrokers said.
Demand for Iraq's Umm Qasr port continued to feature on the freight market although the results of last month's buying tender have yet to emerge.
Glencore quoted for 12,500 tonnes in bags from Thailand to Umm Qasr with Indonesia option for prompt/seven days.
Secretan launched two bagged orders, quoting for 13,200 tonnes from south Brazil to the Red Sea for 10/15 January and a prompt 12,500/14,000 tonnes from Thailand to Umm Qasr with Indonesia option.

Czarnikow Rionda was in the market with two bagged orders and one bulk. It quoted for 12/14,000 tonnes in bags from Thailand to Indonesia for 27 January/5 February and a further prompt same-sized cargo from Buenaventura to Med/west Africa.
Rionda also quoted for 20/22,000 tonnes in bulk from the Philippines to US Gulf/Atlantic for 10/20 January.
CSC was seeking tonnage for two bagged cargoes from New Orleans, the first for 29/30,000 tonnes to Caribs for prompt/onwards and also 5,000 tonnes to Callao for prompt dates.

E D & F Man was active at the start of the week and issued various inquiries. It quoted for 14,000 tonnes min/max bagged sugar from Recife to Algeria for prompt/seven days and 10,000 tonnes min/max bulk from Thailand to Japan for 22/30 January.

Man was also open for 6,000 tonnes preslung bagged sugar from Santander to Lattakia or Tartous for 8/13 January and 12,000 tonnes min/max bagged sugar from Buenaventura to Colombo for 6/20 January. It quoted for 21/24,000 tonnes in bulk from north Brazil to US Gulf/Atlantic for 15/30 January. Cargill mirrored Man's freight activity and quoted four sugar inquiries, mostly from Latin American origins. It quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from north Brazil to Baltic, Black Sea or Egyptian Med for 6/15 January and 3/3,300 tonnes bagged or bulk from Guayaquil to Haiti for prompt/January 10 shipment dates.
Cargill also quoted for just over 33,000 tonnes of bulk sugar, with 15,241 tonnes to be picked up in Punta Morales and 17,848 tonnes in Puerto Quetzal to US Gulf/Atlantic for January 20/February 5.
Lastly, Cargill was in the market for a 14,000-tonne bagged cargo from the European Union, excluding the United Kingdom, to Tunisia/Egypt/Syria for 23/28 January.
Genoc was in the market for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to Casablanca/Med/Black Sea for 16/22 January and 7,500/8,500 tonnes from Salaverry to US Gulf/Atlantic for spot/prompt dates.
It also quoted for a prompt 14,000 tonnes in bags from Buenaventura to east Africa with options including Madagascar, Colombo, Red Sea, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Indonesia.

Shipbrokers said Genoc had fixed, or was close to fixing 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar for prompt dates from south Brazil to a similar range of options -- Mediterranean, Red Sea, Umm Qasr, Pakistan and Colombo.
The only firm business reported came from Amerop, said to have fixed a prompt 8,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from north Brazil to Fray Bentos. Details of the rate have yet to emerge.

Nissho Iwai was said to be in the market for 24,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to Japan for 29 January/7 February and CSR was still open with its bulk order for 30,000 tonnes from Queensland to Crockett for end-January dates.

Shipbrokers said Mauritius Sugar Syndicate (MSS) quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar on its usual run from Port Louis to London for 24/30 January. The last rate achieved by MSS on a similar run was stg 14.25, they said.
Tate & Lyle was open for 12,000 tonnes of bulk raws from Belize to London River or Greenock for 20/25 January.

David Bruce quoted three account orders. Two were for bagged sugar, with one 14/15,000-tonne cargo from Puerto Quetzal to Sri Lanka for 15/20 January and the other for 6/7,000 tonnes from east coast Mexico to west Africa for 18/25 January.
Bruce also quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Thailand to south Korea for 27/31 January.

Other account orders included Greystone Shipping, which quoted for 25/30,000 tonnes in bulk from Cuba to the Egyptian Med for 15/25 January and Ian Richardson & Associates, open for 12,500 tonnes from Kandla to Novorossisk for 8/12 January.
Madre Shipping issued an account order for 12,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Colombo for 10/20 January.
-- Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
